job_function: market risk manager / risk analytics (daily VaR and model-output validation)
control_point: The ISDA standard yield-curve and credit-curve set required by a scheduled risk or valuation batch is complete and sourced from the authorised curve publisher before the batch runs; a missing or unsourced curve blocks the run rather than being back-filled, and the block is cleared by market risk with valuation-control sign-off.

citations.source_name: ISDA CDS Standard Model (open-source model and documentation, administered by S&P Global)
citations.clause: Standard model documentation; ISDA standard rate curves as required inputs

citations.source_name: Basel Framework MAR31, Internal models approach: model requirements
citations.clause: MAR31 qualitative standards: data inputs, model documentation and independent validation

citations.source_name: BCBS d457, Minimum capital requirements for market risk (January 2019)
citations.clause: Internal models approach, general criteria and qualitative standards

consequence_anchor.public_source: Basel Framework MAR31/MAR33 internal-model standards: risk measures produced from incomplete or unvalidated market-data inputs must be re-run, reconciled and reported to supervisors, and repeated input failures bear on model eligibility
consequence_anchor.magnitude_band: qualitative: re-run and reconciliation of the affected risk batch, delayed daily risk reporting, supervisory model-eligibility exposure; no fixed public tariff

commonality_rationale: Every institution computing market or counterparty risk on CDS and rates positions consumes the ISDA standard curve set as a published external input, and every internal-model framework requires complete, sourced inputs before a risk measure is produced; the control is identical across firms because the curve publisher and the model standards are public.
